title: Study dates for 550 more projects
description: Projects without a date were dated from their sources: publication metadata of the page or PDF, a date in the URL, or a date a local model read from the text and quoted word for word (never a page-update, copyright, founding or release date). Dates keep the precision the source gives: a day, a month or a year. Projects with an unknown year fell from 927 to 379.

title: PowSyBl added as a tracked tool
description: PowSyBl, the open-source grid-analysis framework of LF Energy started by RTE, is now tracked: 23 published projects in 11 countries from a country-by-country search of all 199 countries and a deep dive into LF Energy's, Artelys' and grid operators' own pages, each finding checked by an independent validator. Users include RTE, TenneT, Elia, Statnett, Svenska kraftnät, 50Hertz, TransnetBW, the regional coordination centres Coreso and TSCNET, and the Latvian TSO AST. Its code contributors (github.com/powsybl) appear under Who builds the open-source tools.

title: DIgSILENT PowerFactory projects worldwide
description: A country-by-country search of all 199 countries for documented DIgSILENT PowerFactory use, each finding checked by an independent local-model validator. PowerFactory projects grew from 6 to 590 across 123 countries: grid operators' planning and grid-code studies, grid-connection studies by consultancies and developers, and university research. DIgSILENT and its regional offices are not listed as users; personal profiles, job adverts and vague or unnamed organizations were left out.

title: PLEXOS projects from users' and Energy Exemplar's own pages
description: The project deep dive now covers PLEXOS: Energy Exemplar's case studies (credited to the clients, not the vendor), the websites of 21 heavy users such as AEMO, Wärtsilä, NREL, EKC, ECA, the World Bank, Baringa, CCREEE, Chile's Coordinador and ENTSO-E, and every OpenAlex publication reporting PLEXOS use. Published PLEXOS projects grew from 543 to 906 (125 to 137 countries); recurring reports such as AEMO's ESOO and ISP count once per edition.

title: Open Energy Transition projects; summaries for joint projects
description: Every modelling project on Open Energy Transition's website and LinkedIn is now listed (OET's energy-system modelling is PyPSA-based; records whose source does not name the tool say so): OET goes from 7 to 22 PyPSA projects, among them the Wallonia Energy Plan, Ember's European Clean Flexibility Study, NESO's open-source market model and grid planning with Zambia's ZESCO. The summaries of all 278 projects with several organizations were rewritten from the lead organization's view, naming the client or modeller. 677 PyPSA projects are published.

title: One name per organization, structured multi-country studies
description: 127 more name variants across all tools were merged into one name per organization (e.g. Chalmers, Instrat, ONS, OCCTO, Statnett), and 34 rows that repeated the same organization and source were removed. Free-text country fields such as "Pan-European (covers all ENTSO-E member TSOs …)" now name the organization's home country plus the region and countries the study covers, so these studies appear when filtering by any of those countries.

title: PyPSA projects from organizations' own pages and publications
description: A deep dive into the PyPSA work of Open Energy Transition, TU Berlin, KIT, DTU, Aarhus University, PIK and eleven European TSOs (their websites and site searches), plus every OpenAlex publication whose abstract reports using PyPSA, each as one project with all its organizations. Published PyPSA projects grew from 452 to 660; for example TU Berlin now has 54 projects instead of 1, and studies such as ACER's EU-wide flexibility platform and Open-TYNDP list both the client and Open Energy Transition.

title: One record per project
description: Each record is now a project or study, which can name several organizations and countries. Rows citing the same study were joined: 1298 records became 1146 projects, 114 of them with more than one organization. Institutions and Top Users count projects per organization. Filtering by a country also shows the multi-country and global studies that cover it; Grid Decisions lists that country's own projects first, then multi-country, then global, within each impact level.

title: PyPSA users worldwide
description: A country-by-country search of all 199 countries for PyPSA users, plus the PyPSA documentation's users page and OpenAlex publications whose abstracts report using PyPSA. Published PyPSA records grew from 200 to 452 (59 to 82 countries, 194 to 423 institutions); 36 earlier candidate records gained a verified source. New names were matched to the existing institutions, and one organization's PyPSA use in one country is listed once.

title: Tracked tools, organization types and impact-rated grid decisions
description: GridLens now tracks 14 tools (PLEXOS, PyPSA, SDDP, Bid3, PROMOD, PSS/E, PowerFactory, PSCAD, LEAP, TIMES, INTEGRAL, Sienna, Balmorel, Antares), each marked open source or proprietary; 19 records for other tools are no longer published (1065 to 1046 records). Every institution now has one organization type, used by a new Organization type filter and by an impact rating on Grid Decisions (402 high, 275 medium, 369 lower impact). Each record has a one-sentence summary of what was done with the tool, written from its evidence; 212 say the source does not state the purpose. Sources are grouped as industry & government (781) or academic & research (265).

title: Tool categories: capacity expansion, production cost, power flow & dynamics
description: Seven overlapping tool categories became three modelling domains plus Other, each with a description on the Tools & Categories page. Every record was re-read and assigned all domains its evidence describes, so a study can count as both capacity expansion and production cost. Of 1065 published records, 407 are production cost, 425 capacity expansion, 40 power flow & dynamics and 6 other; 78 have more than one. 265 are Unspecified: the source confirms the tool is used but not what for, and tools such as PLEXOS serve several of these purposes.

title: One name per institution and per tool
description: 81 spelling variants of the same organizations were unified (for example Wartsila, Wärtsilä Energy and Wärtsilä North America are now Wärtsilä): 917 to 859 institutions. Model variants are counted under their tool (PyPSA-Eur, PyPSA-GB and others under PyPSA, with the variant kept in the notes), and tool spelling variants were unified (BID3, PSCAD V5): 42 to 32 tools. 9 rows that became exact duplicates (same organization, country, tool and role, or the same source) were merged, keeping every source: 1073 to 1065 published records. Data validation now rejects new name and tool variants.

title: Middle East, Central Asia and Caucasus searched across five modelling tools
description: Middle East, Central Asia and Caucasus grew from 32 to 110 rows and from 16 to 19 countries; confirmed rows rose from 32 to 72 (PLEXOS 51, SDDP 4, PyPSA 15, PROMOD 1, plus 1 for other tools), and confirmed rows with a verbatim quote from 1 to 62.

title: Asia and Oceania searched across five modelling tools
description: Asia and Oceania grew from 124 to 329 rows and from 24 to 27 countries; confirmed rows rose from 124 to 254 (PLEXOS 168, SDDP 16, PyPSA 44, PROMOD 9, plus 17 for other tools), and confirmed rows with a verbatim quote from 31 to 235.

title: Africa searched across five modelling tools
description: Africa grew from 73 to 159 rows and from 35 to 38 countries; confirmed rows rose from 73 to 115 (PLEXOS 85, SDDP 7, PyPSA 15, plus 8 for other tools), and confirmed rows with a verbatim quote from 10 to 78.

title: Europe searched across five modelling tools
description: Europe grew from 129 to 507 rows and from 32 to 40 countries; confirmed rows rose from 129 to 360 (PLEXOS 179, SDDP 30, PyPSA 95, PROMOD 2, Bid3 35, plus 19 for other tools), and confirmed rows with a verbatim quote from 34 to 348.

title: Latin America and the Caribbean searched across five modelling tools
description: Latin America and the Caribbean grew from 40 to 213 rows and from 15 to 30 countries; confirmed rows rose from 40 to 132 (PLEXOS 52, SDDP 58, PyPSA 11, PROMOD 5, plus 6 for Brazil's NEWAVE/DECOMP/DESSEM tool chain), and confirmed rows with a verbatim quote from 6 to 120.

title: North America re-searched across five modelling tools
description: Expanded North America (US, Canada, Mexico) from 85 rows using only PLEXOS and PyPSA to 182 rows across 5 tools (PLEXOS 108, PyPSA 21, PROMOD 27, Bid3 5, SDDP 21); confirmed rows rose from 68 to 119, confirmed rows with quotes from 23 to 97. Countries: US 70→112, Canada 10→49, Mexico 5→21. 27 wrong-organization rows excluded, 9 legacy duplicates merged.

title: UPME (Colombia) confirmed as a PLEXOS direct user
description: Colombia's national energy planning unit's own 2020-2034 expansion plan states it acquired PLEXOS v8.2 — reversing 4 prior independent negative searches.

title: GRIDCo (Ghana Grid Company Limited) added
description: Found via a World Bank procurement contract-award record, distinct from the existing Ghana Energy Commission entry.

title: OCCTO (Japan) reversed from rejected to confirmed
description: OCCTO's own committee materials (2018–2025) describing a multi-year internal PLEXOS-based evaluation outweighed the earlier data-source-only rejection.

title: Tetra Tech / Turkmenistan entry removed
description: Downgraded and removed after a second-pass evidence review found the original source didn't name Turkmenistan specifically.

title: NEXT Group (South Korea) role corrected
description: Changed from consultant_modeler to research_user to reflect its actual co-equal research role in the engagement.

title: 62 new organizations added in a global expansion pass
description: PJM, MISO, NESO (UK), TenneT, KPX, Eskom, and dozens more confirmed across North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa/Middle East.

title: New "subject of study" use cases added
description: GECOL (Libya), Sudan Electricity Holding Company, and EMS (Serbia) added as organizations passively modeled in someone else's PLEXOS study, not direct users themselves.

title: Tracked country coverage expanded to 200 countries
description: Grew from 163 to the full 200-country world list, surfacing gaps in Central Africa, the Pacific, and Caribbean microstates.
